data.name: San Marino
data.summary: From 2026: securities gains taxed at a flat 10%, domestic dividends 5% final, foreign dividends optionally 3% of the net amount. Residents of more than ten continuous years who are not under a special regime also pay IRAFE, 0.2% a year on listed securities and deposits held abroad above EUR 20,000. Succession tax only reaches San Marino-situs assets (assets abroad are outside it by art. 4 of Law 84/1981); for a spouse and children on San Marino assets it is reported as a fixed EUR 100 per heir (low-confidence source). No other wealth tax. Not in the EU: everyone needs a residence permit; an 'atypical residence' regime (art. 16-ter Law 118/2010) taxes foreign income at 7%, with a EUR 10,000 minimum and EUR 100,000 maximum a year, for up to 15 years, and exempts it from IRAFE.

regimes.name: Ordinary tax residence
regimes.description: Residents pay IGR on worldwide income: progressive 9%-35% (35% above EUR 80,000) on ordinary income, with separate flat rates for capital gains (10%), domestic dividends (5% WHT) and, by option, foreign dividends (3% of net) under the 2026 rules.
regimes.eligibility: Tax resident for the majority of the tax period through registered residence, dwelling or centre of vital interests in San Marino; requires a San Marino residence permit for non-citizens.

capital_gains.summary: From tax year 2026 capital gains of individuals on shares, other participations and financial instruments (domestic or foreign) are taxed separately at a flat 10% (Law 166/2013 art. 41 and art. 13 as replaced by Law 141/2025). Real estate gains are taxable only if the property was held 5 years or less; the main home and inherited property are exempt.
capital_gains.exemptions_thresholds: Real estate held more than 5 years, main residence, and property received by inheritance are exempt. Losses on securities offset gains of the same year only; no carry-forward (art. 41(6)). LIFO for securities acquired at different times; weighted average cost within an intermediary.
capital_gains.important_exceptions: 2026 reform (Law 141/2025, approved 5 November 2025): the separate-taxation article was rewritten. Pre-2026 tax return forms referred to a 2% substitute tax on financial instruments; how gains were taxed before 2026 was not fully verified. Some secondary sources still claim gains on shares held 12+ months are exempt; that participation exemption applies to companies, not to individuals under art. 41.

open_questions: Whether a delegated decree has adjusted the 10% rate (art. 13(4) allows changes by decreto delegato).
Pre-2026 treatment of individuals' securities gains (to describe the change precisely).
capital_gains.rate_basis: Art. 13(1)(b) and 13(2)(b) of Law 166/2013 as replaced by art. 4 of Law 141/2025 (in force from tax period 2026): 'plusvalenze patrimoniali di cui all'articolo 41' taxed separately at 10%. Art. 41(1)(b)-(c) covers disposals of shares, participations and financial instruments; (d) covers sale of a business. Real estate: 0 assumes the property was held more than 5 years (art. 41(1)(a)); a sale within 5 years is taxed at 10%. Via a San Marino intermediary the 10% is withheld as a final tax on 31 December; for foreign-source gains the taxpayer may opt for progressive IGR instead (only useful for small amounts).
capital_gains.professional_trader: Gains realised within a business (reddito d'impresa) are business income, taxed at 17% (18% for 2026-2030) under art. 13(2)(a) for operatori economici; not researched in detail.
capital_gains.holding_period_rules: None for securities. Real estate: taxable only if held 5 years or less (donor's holding period added for gifted property).
capital_gains.foreign_assets: Residents are taxed on worldwide income; gains on financial instruments issued by non-residents are taxed at 10% like domestic ones.

dividends.summary: Dividends from San Marino companies: 5% final withholding for individuals (art. 103(6) Law 166/2013). Foreign dividends: by option, separate taxation at 3% of the amount received after foreign withholding ('netto frontiera'); otherwise they enter progressive IGR (9%-35%) with a foreign tax credit.
dividends.exemptions_thresholds: Collected as a final withholding when received through a San Marino intermediary; the taxpayer may treat it as an advance and opt into progressive taxation.
dividends.important_exceptions: Under the progressive option, foreign tax is credited up to the IGR attributable to that income. Interest on foreign bonds: 10% of net amount by option; interest on foreign bank accounts: 13%.

open_questions: Treaty list and whether the US has any tax agreement with San Marino covering dividends.
dividends.rate_basis: Domestic: 5% final WHT. Foreign: 3% on the 'netto frontiera', the foreign income as received net of tax paid in the source state (art. 13(1)(g), 13(2)(e) and 13(3) of Law 166/2013 as replaced by art. 4 of Law 141/2025, read 2026-10-16). There is no credit: the source tax is deducted from the base (foreign_tax_credit 'deduction'). Example: US dividend 100, US WHT 30 (no treaty) -> San Marino tax 3% x 70 = 2.1, total 32.1%.
dividends.withholding_outbound: 5% WHT on dividends paid by San Marino companies to individuals, resident or not; no WHT when the recipient declares it is not acting for an individual (art. 103(6)). Treaties may reduce it.
dividends.treaty_network: Small network (e.g. Italy: 15% portfolio dividends, 0% for 10%/12-month corporate holdings). No income tax treaty with the US, so US dividends suffer 30% US WHT. Network size not verified.
dividends.holding_company_notes: San Marino companies exclude 95% of dividends from non-resident subsidiaries held 12+ months (participation exemption); not verified for 2026.

wealth_tax.summary: IRAFE (imposta per il riequilibrio delle attivita finanziarie estere): 0.2% a year on the market value at 31 December of financial assets held abroad, directly or indirectly, by an individual resident for more than ten continuous years and not under a special regime on foreign income. The first EUR 20,000 is excluded (the Ufficio Tributario computes the tax on the excess). Shares of foreign non-listed companies, shareholder loans, precious metals, foreign banknotes, life and health insurance policies, pension funds and non-financial assets are excluded. No other annual tax on wealth. A new arrival pays nothing for ten years; atypical residents never pay it.
wealth_tax.exemptions_thresholds: EUR 20,000 of foreign financial assets excluded (art. 4 para. 3 Law 207/2021; circular Prot. 61702/2022: tax on the excess). Tax of EUR 10 or less is not due (art. 4 para. 5-bis, added by art. 17 Law 94/2022). The rate may be changed by delegated decree (art. 4 para. 4).
wealth_tax.eligibility_conditions: Individuals resident in San Marino for more than ten continuous years (art. 17 Law 94/2022, replacing the original five) who are not under a special regime on foreign income such as the atypical residence (art. 4 para. 2 Law 207/2021). The text says 'o' (or) between the two conditions, but the Ufficio Tributario circular reads them cumulatively ('e').
wealth_tax.important_exceptions: Assets repatriated to San Marino before the 2021 DAPEF deadline were excluded for 2021 only. Self-assessed in the DAPEF declaration; payment deadline for tax year 2023 was 2 October 2024 (circular of 27 May 2024), so the tax was still being collected in 2024. Not found: any repeal in Law 141/2025 or the 2026 budget (not searched line by line).

open_questions: IRAFE in force in 2026? Law 207/2021 art. 4 and the 2024 circular were read; no repeal found in Law 141/2025, but neither the 2024-2026 budget laws nor the delegated decrees were searched line by line.

Art. 4 para. 2 as amended reads 'residente ... da oltre dieci anni continuativi o non assoggettata a regimi speciali' (or). The circular of March 2022 (before the amendment) reads 'da 5 anni continuativi e non assoggettati'; a firm summary (HLB) reads the amendment as ten years. Cumulative ten years is assumed.
Whether the EUR 20,000 exclusion is per taxpayer (spouses holding jointly each get it) was not stated.
Existence and level of any recurring real estate levy.

IRAFE trigger: art. 4(2) Law 207/2021 as amended by art. 17 Law 94/2022 reads 'da oltre dieci anni continuativi o non assoggettata a regimi speciali' (literally 'or'); the Ufficio Tributario circulars read it cumulatively (over 10 years of registered residence and no special regime), which is what is modelled. On the literal reading a new resident outside a special regime would pay it from the start.

components.name: IRAFE on financial assets held abroad
components.notes: 0.2% of the market value at 31 December above EUR 20,000 (art. 4 paras. 3-4 Law 207/2021). Applies only after ten continuous years of residence and never to atypical residents: the model's wealth tax runs from year 1 and so overcharges years 1-10 (see open questions).

wealth_tax.property_tax_note: Not verified whether a recurring municipal property tax exists. Residents must also declare their financial assets and company holdings held abroad each year (DAPEF; reporting).

inheritance.summary: Succession tax (Law 84/1981) applies only to assets located in San Marino: art. 4 exempts all assets located abroad. For a spouse and descendants it is reported to be a symbolic fixed EUR 100 per heir regardless of value, plus 0.10% stamp duty on the net estate and, for San Marino real estate, 1% transcription and 0.40% cadastral transfer tax. Foreign assets of a resident are outside its scope.
inheritance.exemptions_thresholds: Fixed EUR 100 per heir for spouse and direct-line relatives. Progressive rates apply only to more distant relatives (5%-30% uncles/nephews, 8%-35% great-uncles, 10%-35% others).
inheritance.important_exceptions: Source is a 2015 article by the head of the San Marino Registry Office describing the then-current practice; the 1981 statute's own tariff (in lire, 1%-20% for direct line) was evidently superseded, but the amending act was not located. Inherited real estate passing to foreigners also bears 'imposta di cinquina' (5% for direct line, 10% otherwise) under art. 1 of Law 84/1981; its current status is unverified.

open_questions: The EUR 100 fixed tax for spouse and direct-line heirs on San Marino-situs assets comes from a 2015 article by the head of the Registry Office; the 1981 statute's tariff (lire) has evidently been superseded, but the amending act was not located. It only affects San Marino-situs assets; foreign assets are exempt by statute (art. 4).
Gift tax / registration tax on gifts to children.
Current status of the 'imposta di cinquina' (5% direct line) on San Marino real estate inherited by foreigners (art. 1 Law 84/1981).
inheritance.spouse_note: Spouse shares bear a symbolic fixed EUR 100 per heir regardless of value, plus 0.10% stamp duty on the net estate and, on San Marino real estate, 1% transcription and 0.40% cadastral tax; only San Marino-situs assets are taxed (Law 84/1981, as described by the Registry Office in 2015).
inheritance.gift_tax: Not verified. One Italian advisory page states there is no gift or inheritance tax; registration taxes on gift deeds and the treatment of large gifts of foreign securities were not confirmed.
inheritance.business_relief: Not needed for direct-line heirs given the fixed amount.
inheritance.foreign_assets: Situs principle: art. 3 of Law 84/1981 taxes San Marino immovables whatever the deceased's domicile or nationality, and art. 4 expressly exempts movable and immovable assets located outside San Marino and credits not enforceable there. A foreign securities portfolio passing to children is therefore outside the tax (statute read 2026-10-15). Read again 2026-10-16: art. 4 no. 1 'Non sono soggetti a imposta di successione: i beni immobili e mobili posti fuori del territorio della Repubblica'; art. 3 taxes immovables in San Marino whatever the domicile or nationality. The tax file therefore scores the regime as local_assets_only.
inheritance.domicile_rules: No residence-based scope. The heirs' country of residence may tax them.

regimes.name: Residenza atipica (reduced taxation on foreign income)
regimes.description: Residenza atipica soggetta a regime fiscale agevolato (art. 16-ter Law 118/2010, introduced by art. 69 Law 223/2020): a substitute tax replacing IGR on income produced abroad, 7% of the 'netto frontiera' (income net of foreign tax), with a minimum of EUR 10,000 and a maximum of EUR 100,000 for each fiscal year, payable in one instalment with the IGR balance. It is not a fixed lump sum: below the cap the tax is 7% of the foreign income. It ends 15 years after the first tax period (revocable earlier, and lost on any missed or partial payment). Income from San Marino sources and the IRAFE position are outside it: atypical residents are not liable to IRAFE.
regimes.eligibility: Natural persons who have never been tax resident in San Marino (or whose residence was not yet consolidated when the article took effect), who produce income abroad and are not caught by art. 17 paras. 1-2 of the residence law. Application to the Department of Foreign Affairs with a EUR 1,000 fee, a passport copy, a purchase or lease contract for a dwelling, certificates from the previous country of residence, a declaration of nationalities and residences of the last 5 years and proof of sufficient resources; the Congress of State decides within 60 days and its decision cannot be challenged. At most 100 permits a year (not counting extended family members). Spouse and family members listed in art. 16 para. 3-bis can be included on request. Until residence is consolidated (ten years from registration) the holder cannot take public-sector employment, receives no public benefits tied to residence and must carry private or ISS health cover (art. 16-ter paras. 3-14 Law 118/2010 as in Law 223/2020 art. 69).
regimes.duration_note: Ends 15 years after the first tax period of validity (art. 16-ter para. 8): the ordinary regime, including IRAFE after ten years of residence, then applies.

capital_gains.summary: Gains on foreign securities of a holder of the atypical residence are covered by the 7% substitute tax on the net-of-foreign-tax income, within a EUR 10,000 minimum and EUR 100,000 maximum a year per taxpayer (art. 16-ter para. 2 Law 118/2010). Below the cap there is no cut-off: each further euro of foreign gain pays 7%; once the tax has reached EUR 100,000 further foreign gains pay nothing.

prime_rent_monthly.description: Median of the two largest homes for long-term rent in the Republic of San Marino on Mioaffitto.it (an Italian portal aggregating agency ads) on 2026-10-15: a furnished 220 m² detached villa in Torraccia (Domagnano) with 3 double bedrooms, a tavern level and garden (EUR 2,300/month) and a furnished 260 m² detached villa in Casole (Città di San Marino) with 3 bedrooms on a 1,000 m² plot (EUR 2,000/month; its text also says 'in vendita', so it may be offered for sale too). The page listed 11 San Marino rentals (Domagnano, Borgo Maggiore, Città, Dogana); none had 4–5 bedrooms, and the other large units were flats of 110–168 m² at EUR 1,000–1,500. Very thin sample; 3-bedroom villas are used as the closest available proxy for a prime family home. Checked 2026-10-15 against the upper-middle-class standard.

intl_school_annual_fee.description: San Marino has no international school; this is the International School of Bologna (IB Continuum school, about 135 km by road from San Marino, the nearest verified IB school a San Marino family would realistically use), 2026–27 annual tuition for Grades 11–12: EUR 21,870, plus an annual registration fee of EUR 1,000 (Grades 11–12) and a one-off EUR 1,500 admission fee. IB exam fees, books and insurance are included; lunch is extra. Daily commuting from San Marino is not realistic, so in practice this implies boarding/relocation or an Italian or Sammarinese private school instead.

succession.summary: Succession law is not codified, and children and the spouse are protected by a reserved share whose size was not confirmed. The Hague Trusts Convention is in force and San Marino has its own trust law. Foundations were not confirmed.
succession.reserved_share: A reserved part (portio debita) exists for legitimate heirs under San Marino's common-law rules, with spouse rights in intestacy under Law 49/1986 (usufruct of the whole estate plus a child-sized share when there are children). Sizes of the reserve were not confirmed.
succession.foreign_law_note: San Marino private international law on succession was not found. Not under the EU Regulation.
succession.trust_note: The Hague Trusts Convention is in force since 1 August 2006 (HCCH table: accession 28 April 2005). San Marino has its own trust statute (a secondary source says domestic trusts are governed by San Marino law with a specialised court). Fiduciary contracts also exist. The existence and scope of a foundation law were not confirmed; the entry 'limited' is a placeholder.
open_questions: Size of the reserve and the conflict rule for succession were not found.
Trust statute citation (law number and date) was not read.
Foundations: no source found; 'limited' is not backed by a source.
Trust/foundation availability marked unclear: no statute was found, which does not show that none exists.

assumptions: The family are EU citizens with no previous San Marino residence, so they can apply for the atypical residence (art. 16-ter para. 1 Law 118/2010) and, failing that, for another permit; San Marino is not in the EU and every permit needs a decision of the Congress of State. The ordinary residence route (elective residence) was not researched against the statute.

The portfolio is in one name for the checks. The atypical substitute tax is charged for each person on that person's foreign income within the band, so a couple splitting the portfolio equally pays the same 7% in total as long as neither reaches the EUR 100,000 cap; whether the EUR 10,000 minimum also falls on an extended spouse or child with no foreign income was not settled (see open questions).

Ordinary regime: the family elects separate taxation of foreign dividends (3% on the net amount); the alternative is progressive IGR (9% to 35%) with a credit for foreign tax, which a 600,000 dividend income would not choose.

IRAFE is scored as a wealth tax on all foreign financial assets above EUR 20,000. The portfolio is held at foreign brokers (not repatriated), so no part is excluded. Italian-held or San Marino-held assets would not be 'abroad'.

Deaths in years 30 and 60 fall after both the 15-year atypical regime and the ten-year IRAFE waiting period, so the ordinary rules always apply at death. The inheritance checks assume a foreign securities portfolio; San Marino-situs assets (the home) were left out.

Not offered as paths: a San Marino holding company (IGR 17%, 18% for 2026-2030, with a 95% exclusion for qualifying foreign dividends that was not verified for 2026), a San Marino trust and a foundation. The family already pays 3% on dividends and 10% on gains personally, and the portfolio is already outside succession tax, so a company brings no estate advantage and adds a layer of 17-18% tax; trusts and foundations are not commonly used for a listed portfolio in San Marino as far as could be found.
open_questions: Needs an engine change: the atypical substitute tax is 7% of net foreign income but never less than EUR 10,000 and never more than EUR 100,000 for each taxpayer and fiscal year (art. 16-ter para. 2 Law 118/2010). The tax file can hold only the 7% rate on foreign dividends and gains. For a portfolio with more than about EUR 1.43m of net foreign income a year, the cap makes further income tax-free; and a family member with little foreign income may owe the minimum. The engine needs a floor and a ceiling on a substitute tax, per taxpayer.

The 'o' in art. 4 para. 2 as amended ('residente ... da oltre dieci anni continuativi o non assoggettata a regimi speciali') can be read as an alternative, which would make IRAFE apply to every resident outside a special regime from year 1. The circular written before the amendment reads the two conditions together (five years then). A ruling on the ten-year text should be sought.
IRAFE in 2026: the payment deadline for tax year 2023 is in the circular of 27 May 2024; no repeal in Law 141/2025 was seen in the parts read, but the 2025 and 2026 budget laws were not searched.
Whether the EUR 20,000 exclusion of IRAFE applies once per taxpayer or once per spouse; the checks use one taxpayer.

Succession: the EUR 100 fixed tax for a spouse and children on San Marino assets rests on a 2015 article; the 1981 tariff (1% to 20% in lire for the direct line) and the 5% 'imposta di cinquina' on immovables passing to foreigners (art. 1) may still apply to the EUR 5m home, which the check excludes.

Trust: a San Marino trust is a taxpayer on 80% of the income received, or 10% if the trustee reinvests for 24 months and elects (Toccaceli Bronzetti, Trust Taxation in San Marino); the rate was not stated in the page and a 15% withholding applies to attributions to non-resident beneficiaries. If that rate is the 17-18% corporate rate, an accumulating trust would pay about 1.7% on income, a possible reason to add a path. Not researched further.
Whether Law 141/2025 changed art. 16-ter Law 118/2010 or its band, and whether an atypical resident may elect the 3% dividend option instead of the 7% regime, were not found.

paths.name: Holding the portfolio personally (ordinary residence)
paths.note: From 2026 foreign dividends can be taxed at 3% of the amount net of the foreign withholding (art. 13 Law 166/2013 as replaced by Law 141/2025) and gains on shares at a flat 10%. After ten continuous years of residence IRAFE adds 0.2% a year on foreign financial assets above EUR 20,000 (art. 4 Law 207/2021, art. 17 Law 94/2022). Assets abroad are outside San Marino succession tax (art. 4 no. 1 Law 84/1981).

paths.name: Atypical residence (7% substitute tax on foreign income, 15 years, then ordinary rules)
paths.regime: Residenza atipica (reduced taxation on foreign income)
paths.note: Art. 16-ter Law 118/2010 (art. 69 Law 223/2020): a 7% substitute tax on income produced abroad net of foreign tax, between EUR 10,000 and EUR 100,000 a year, replaces the IGR on foreign dividends and gains, and the holder is not liable to IRAFE. It ends 15 years after the first tax period; the standard regime, with IRAFE (more than ten years resident), then applies, so both deaths (years 30 and 60) fall under the ordinary rules. Granted by the Congress of State at its discretion, at most 100 a year.

immigration.name: San Marino
immigration.summary: San Marino is not in the EU and has no free movement for EU citizens: everyone, EU citizens included, needs a permit or residence from the San Marino authorities, and entry is through Italy (Schengen). All residence is discretionary and capped. EU citizens: the cheapest open route is the pensioner residence (income of EUR 50,000 a year or EUR 300,000 in assets, 6% tax on pension) if retired, otherwise the reduced-tax regime for foreign income (EUR 1,000 fee, 7% tax). US and other citizens: the reduced-tax regime for foreign income or elective residence (property of EUR 500,000 or deposit of EUR 600,000); pensioner residence is open only to Swiss and listed countries. An EU association agreement is due to be signed on 19 October 2026 and is not in force.
immigration.naturalisation: Since Law 27 of 25 February 2026 (amending Law 114/2000): 20 continuous years of registered and effective residence (10 for a spouse or civil partner of a citizen), Italian at B1 level and a test on San Marino history and institutions; renouncing the old nationality is no longer required. Not an entitlement.
immigration.dual_citizenship_note: The 2026 reform removed the obligation to renounce the previous citizenship (committee report of 10 December 2025 and Regolamento 4/2026 implementing the law). The law text itself was not read.

routes.name: Elective residence (residenza elettiva)
routes.limited_places: Discretionary: the Congresso di Stato decides, no right to it; at most 50 a year (secondary applicants excluded)
routes.summary: Residence for a foreigner who buys a home in San Marino for at least EUR 500,000 or locks up EUR 600,000 in San Marino state securities for 10 years. The Congresso di Stato may refuse without giving a reason that can be appealed.
routes.requirements: Law 118/2010, art. 16-bis (introduced by Law 94/2017): (a) buy a building (finished before 31 May 2017, or to be renovated or unfinished) for at least EUR 500,000 for own use, where up to EUR 150,000 of completion, renovation or rebuilding costs may count towards the sum; or (b) a non-interest-bearing deposit of at least EUR 600,000 in San Marino state securities or a State-set-up fund, tied up 10 years. Proof of sufficient means for the family, clean criminal record, full private health insurance at own cost (no state health cover), no employment in the wider public sector, no public benefits until residence consolidates after 10 years. Not available with a conviction or pending case over 1 year, or with a Schengen entry ban (arts. 17). Purchase deed or deposit must be completed within 3 months of the grant or the residence is revoked. Property purchase pays 8% registration tax (art. 16-bis c.5). Entry to San Marino is through Italy; a Schengen visa may be needed.
routes.investment_options: Property of EUR 500,000 or more (EUR 350,000 building plus up to EUR 150,000 works counts), or a EUR 600,000 10-year deposit in San Marino state securities, or both.
routes.fees_note: EUR 1,000 application fee; EUR 10,000 non-refundable one-off fee if the deposit option is used; EUR 20,000 one-off per secondary applicant (spouse, children up to 25 dependent, disabled child). Property option also pays 8% registration tax.
routes.physical_presence: Genuine habitual residence; art. 17 revokes residence if habitual residence in San Marino lapses for over 6 months
routes.processing_time: Congresso di Stato decides within 60 days of a complete application (art. 16-bis c.4)
routes.family: Spouse and children up to 25 who are dependent (or disabled children) can be added for EUR 20,000 each; children born later are included free.
routes.tax_note: Residence does not by itself set the tax position; San Marino levies ordinary personal income tax on residents. The reduced-tax regimes below are separate residence types.

routes.name: Atypical residence for pensioners (EU citizens)
routes.limited_places: Discretionary: decided by the parliamentary Foreign Affairs Committee; at most 249 a year under art. 16-quater c.12 (some cases excluded from the count)
routes.summary: Residence for retired people from EU countries who have never lived in San Marino, with a flat 6% substitute tax on pension income for 10 consecutive years, renewable.
routes.requirements: Law 118/2010, art. 16-quater: pensioner from an EU country; demonstrable gross income of at least EUR 50,000 a year or movable assets of at least EUR 300,000 (text in the April 2024 consolidated version; see open questions on the proposed rise to EUR 120,000 / 500,000); never previously resident in San Marino; preliminary purchase or rental contract for a home conditional on the grant (renting a room shared with unrelated people is not accepted); proof of means for the family; a current account at a San Marino bank; health costs at own charge; no wider-public-sector job and no public benefits until residence consolidates after 10 years. 6% applies whether or not a double-tax treaty exists; 3% for retired officials of international organisations with income of at least EUR 100,000.
routes.investment_options: Alternative to the income test: movable assets of at least EUR 300,000.
routes.fees_note: EUR 1,000 application fee (diritto erariale). No other government fee found.
routes.physical_presence: Genuine habitual residence in San Marino; no day count published
routes.processing_time: Committee decides within 120 days of a complete application (art. 16-quater c.4)
routes.family: Spouse and dependent children up to 25 can be added as secondary applicants.
routes.tax_note: 6% flat substitute tax on pension income for 10 consecutive years, renewable (art. 16-quater c.2 and c.8); 3% for retired officials of international organisations with income of at least EUR 100,000.

routes.name: Atypical residence with reduced tax regime (income earned abroad)
routes.limited_places: Discretionary: the Congresso di Stato decides; at most 100 a year per the April 2024 consolidated text (changeable yearly by decree)
routes.summary: Residence for people who earn their income abroad and were never tax resident in San Marino. A 7% substitute tax applies to foreign income, with a minimum of EUR 10,000 and a maximum of EUR 100,000 a year.
routes.requirements: Law 118/2010, art. 16-ter (Law 223/2020, arts. 69-70): never fiscally resident in San Marino (or residence not yet consolidated when the article entered into force); income produced abroad; preliminary home purchase or rental contract conditional on the grant; proof of sufficient means for the family; certificates of residence, criminal record and pending cases; health costs at own charge; no wider-public-sector job and no public benefits. The tax regime ends after 15 years at most and is lost for non-payment. No minimum income or investment is set by law.
routes.fees_note: EUR 1,000 application fee. The substitute tax is not a fee.
routes.physical_presence: Genuine habitual residence in San Marino; no day count published
routes.processing_time: Congresso di Stato decides within 60 days of a complete application
routes.family: Spouse and dependent children can be added as secondary applicants.
routes.tax_note: 7% substitute tax on 'netto frontiera' foreign income, minimum EUR 10,000 and maximum EUR 100,000 a year, payable in one sum; regime lasts at most 15 years.

routes.name: Residence for entrepreneurs, executives and investors in a San Marino business
routes.limited_places: Discretionary: granted by the Foreign Affairs Committee on the Congresso di Stato's proposal after a mandatory Gendarmerie opinion
routes.summary: Residence or an ordinary permit for people who invest capital in a San Marino business with job and property commitments, hold a senior role in a San Marino company, bank or hospital, or run a project of strategic interest. No fixed investment sum is set in the law.
routes.requirements: Law 118/2010, art. 16 c.3: senior role in health, bank, insurance or financial institutions or in a company with many employees; investment of capital in a business (existing or being set up) with employment guarantees (hires from the job-placement lists, partners and their relatives not counted) and linked property investment; strategic projects; donations of cultural or social assets; internationally recognised merit in science, art, culture or sport. The residence lasts for the duration of the activity and consolidates after 10 years (c.3-ter). Unless working, applicants need own means and health insurance with at least EUR 30,000 cover for the first 24 months (c.3-quater). Amounts for the capital and number of hires are set in the Congresso di Stato's decisions and were not found in an official source.
routes.physical_presence: Genuine habitual residence; residence is revoked if habitual residence lapses for over 6 months
routes.family: Spouse, children up to 25 who are dependent, and disabled dependent children can be added (art. 16 c.3-bis).

routes.name: Employment in San Marino (work permit and residence permit)
routes.limited_places: Permits are issued within yearly entry quotas set by delegated decree
routes.summary: An employer must obtain a work clearance from the Ufficio del Lavoro; the Gendarmeria then issues a residence permit for work valid up to 12 months. Permits are seasonal or temporary and renewable, not a path to residence.
routes.requirements: Law 118/2010, arts. 10 and 12: work permit from the Ufficio del Lavoro within the quotas, employer declaration of housing and return travel cost, seasonal or temporary permit up to 12 months continuous, renewable, interrupted after three consecutive renewals. Cross-border workers cannot get this permit. Non-Schengen nationals need a non-tourist Schengen entry visa where required. Highly skilled and managerial staff may instead be given ordinary residence under art. 16 c.3 (see the entrepreneur route). No digital nomad visa found.
routes.physical_presence: Place of work and housing in San Marino

open_questions: EU association agreement: signing planned 19 October 2026 (EEAS), Council approved signing and provisional application on 16 July 2026; no source confirms it is in force on 2026-10-17. Its effect on residence or free movement of persons was not found and is not assumed.

Pensioner thresholds: Decree 26/2025 (in force 20 February 2025) raised them to EUR 120,000 income or EUR 500,000 movable assets, but the ratifying Decree 77/2025 (22 May 2025) marks that article 'abrogato'. Figures here follow the April 2024 consolidated text (EUR 50,000 / EUR 300,000); secondary sources report EUR 120,000 income and EUR 300,000 assets in San Marino banks from 28 April 2025. Needs a current consolidated text.
List of non-EU countries eligible for pensioner residence (Congresso di Stato regulation) not found; whether the US is on it is unknown, so the US is left off pensioner residence.
Annual caps (50 elective, 100 atypical tax regime) come from the April 2024 consolidated text; the 249 cap for pensioners is from Decree 77/2025. Later yearly decrees were not checked.
Capital and hiring figures for entrepreneur residence (art. 16 c.3 c) not found in an official source; Filodiritto (2022) mentions property of EUR 200,000 to 300,000 and 2 to 4 employees.

Simplified residence (Law 71/2013, 5 permanent hires plus EUR 300,000 property) and economic residence (Law 115/2017, EUR 75,000 deposit, 51% of a company) are reported only by a 2022 secondary source and were not verified or included.
Processing time for residence permits and renewal period of the first permit not sourced; physical-presence day counts are not published.
Law 27/2026 text not read; 20-year residence and B1 Italian come from the implementing regulation and the committee report.
